category: Cloud II: Cloud Storage, Channels, Databins, Tasks & Persistence
description: Cloud object storage and sharing (publish, share, save, cloud expressions and symbols, logging), the channel messaging framework, Wolfram Data Drop databins, asynchronous and scheduled task management (SessionSubmit, LocalSubmit, CloudSubmit, TaskObject), and local/persistent storage (LocalObject, LocalSymbol, PersistentSymbol, InitializationValue).

tools.name: CloudPublish
tools.description: Deploys an expression, notebook or file to the cloud with Permissions -> "Public" and a viewer-friendly presentation (published notebooks are rendered as web pages), returning a CloudObject URL. It is the one-call way to share a report or interactive notebook with anyone; CloudDeploy is the general form with private permissions by default.
tools.usage:
CloudPublish[expr]
CloudPublish[expr, "path"]
CloudPublish[notebookObject]
CloudPublish[expr, opts]

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Expression, notebook or file to publish.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Optional named location in the cloud.

tools.name: CloudShare
tools.description: Shares an existing CloudObject with specific users (by Wolfram ID / email) or a PermissionsGroup, optionally with given permission levels, and sends a notification email. Use it to grant collaborators access to private deployments without making them public.
tools.usage:
CloudShare[obj]
CloudShare[obj, "user@example.com"]
CloudShare[obj, {"user1", "user2"}]
CloudShare[obj, PermissionsGroup["team"]]
CloudShare[obj, users -> {"Read", "Execute"}]

parameters.name: users
parameters.description: Wolfram IDs, email addresses or PermissionsGroup.

tools.name: PermissionsGroup
tools.description: Represents a named group of users for cloud permissions: CreatePermissionsGroup makes a group, AddUsers / RemoveUsers / SetUsers manage membership, and the group can be used in Permissions -> {PermissionsGroup["name"] -> {"Read", "Execute"}} of CloudDeploy or in CloudShare. PermissionsGroups lists the groups you own.
tools.usage:
PermissionsGroup["name"]
CreatePermissionsGroup["name", {"user1", "user2"}]
AddUsers[PermissionsGroup["name"], {"user3"}]
RemoveUsers[PermissionsGroup["name"], {"user1"}]
CloudDeploy[expr, Permissions -> {PermissionsGroup["name"] -> "Read"}]
PermissionsGroups[]

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Group name (owned by the current cloud user).

tools.name: CloudSave
tools.description: Saves the definitions (DownValues, OwnValues, options, messages) of one or more symbols to a cloud object, like Save but in the cloud, so that CloudGet[obj] restores them in another session or on another machine. Use it to share function libraries between local and cloud kernels.
tools.usage:
CloudSave[symbol]
CloudSave[{s1, s2, ...}]
CloudSave[symbol, "path"]
CloudGet[CloudObject["path"]]

tools.name: CloudExpression
tools.description: A cloud-stored expression that supports in-place part updates without downloading the whole structure: CreateCloudExpression makes one, ce["key"] and ce[["key"]] read parts, ce["key"] = value or AppendTo[ce["list"], x] modify parts atomically on the server. Ideal as a lightweight shared key-value/JSON store for deployed APIs and forms.
tools.usage:
ce = CreateCloudExpression[<|"count" -> 0, "log" -> {}|>]
ce = CreateCloudExpression[expr, "name"]
ce["count"]
ce["count"] = 5
ce["count"]++
AppendTo[ce["log"], Now]
CloudExpression["name"]
DeleteObject[ce]

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Initial expression (typically an Association or list).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Optional name for later retrieval with CloudExpression["name"].

tools.notes: Part operations are atomic and much faster than CloudGet/CloudPut round trips; $CloudExpressionBase sets the default location.

tools.name: CloudSymbol
tools.description: CloudSymbol["name"] is a symbol whose value lives in the cloud: assigning to it stores the value, evaluating it fetches the current value, so it acts as a persistent global variable shared between sessions, deployed APIs and scheduled tasks. $CloudSymbolBase sets where the values are stored.
tools.usage:
CloudSymbol["name"]
CloudSymbol["name"] = value
CloudSymbol["name"] += 1
CloudSymbol["name"] =.
tools.notes: Each access is a network round trip; for structured data with frequent partial updates prefer CloudExpression.

tools.name: CloudObjects
tools.description: Lists the cloud objects in your cloud account or a given directory (optionally filtered by type such as "Notebook", "API", "Form", "Task"), and CloudDirectory / SetCloudDirectory manage the current cloud working directory used by relative object names. Use them to inventory and clean up deployments.
tools.usage:
CloudObjects[]
CloudObjects["dir"]
CloudObjects[CloudDirectory[], "API"]
CloudObjects[Permissions -> "Public"]
CloudDirectory[]
SetCloudDirectory["dir"]
tools.example:
apis = CloudObjects[CloudDirectory[], "API"];
DeleteObject /@ CloudObjects["tmp"] (* remove scratch deployments *)

tools.name: CloudLoggingData
tools.description: Retrieves access logs and usage statistics for deployed cloud objects (requests, response times, requester locations, credits used) over a period, as a Dataset-like structure. Use it to monitor APIs and forms you have deployed.
tools.usage:
CloudLoggingData[]
CloudLoggingData[obj]
CloudLoggingData[obj, period]
CloudLoggingData[obj, "Daily"]
CloudLoggingData[obj, {date1, date2}]

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: "Day", "Week", "Month", a date range or granularity string.

tools.name: CloudAccountData
tools.description: Gives information about the connected cloud account: storage and cloud-credit usage and limits, subscription type, and user data; $CloudUserID, $WolframID and $CloudBase identify the account and cloud endpoint. Use it to check quotas before large uploads.
tools.usage:
CloudAccountData[]
CloudAccountData["prop"]
CloudAccountData[{"CloudStorageUsed", "CloudStorageLimit"}]

tools.name: CloudDisconnect
tools.description: Disconnects the session from the Wolfram Cloud (the inverse of CloudConnect), clearing the stored authentication so subsequent cloud operations prompt again or fail; $CloudConnected reports the current state. Useful in scripts that switch accounts or must end a session cleanly.
tools.usage:
CloudDisconnect[]
$CloudConnected
CloudConnect["user", "password"]

tools.name: AutoRefreshed
tools.description: AutoRefreshed[expr, schedule] deployed to the cloud is recomputed on the given schedule (e.g. "Hourly", Quantity[10, "Minutes"], a DateObject-based spec) and cached, so viewers get a fresh but precomputed result - the right tool for dashboards that pull data periodically without recomputing on every request (contrast Delayed, which recomputes per request).
tools.usage:
CloudDeploy[AutoRefreshed[expr, schedule]]
CloudDeploy[AutoRefreshed[expr, schedule, fmt]]

tools.name: CloudFunction
tools.description: Wraps a function so that it is evaluated in the cloud when called locally (arguments are sent up, the result returned), or references a deployed function by CloudObject. Use it to offload heavy or cloud-data-dependent computations from a lightweight local session, or to call your own APIs as ordinary functions.
tools.usage:
cf = CloudFunction[f]
cf[args]
CloudFunction[CloudObject["path"]]
CloudDeploy[CloudFunction[f], "name"]

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Function or CloudObject of a deployed function.

tools.name: ExternalBundle
tools.description: ExternalBundle[{"name1" -> expr1, ...}] deployed to the cloud produces a page bundling several deployable objects (APIs, forms, data) under one URL with a listing; EmbeddedHTML and EmbeddedService similarly embed raw HTML or third-party services (YouTube, maps) inside a deployed page or notebook. Used to package multi-endpoint cloud services and rich pages.
tools.usage: CloudDeploy[ExternalBundle[{"api" -> APIFunction[...], "form" -> FormFunction[...]}]] EmbeddedHTML["html"] EmbeddedService["YouTube", "videoId"]

tools.name: CreateChannel
tools.description: Creates a cloud message channel (a named pub/sub endpoint) returning a ChannelObject; ChannelSend publishes messages to it and ChannelListen subscribes. Channels give real-time push messaging between kernels, notebooks, deployed APIs and external HTTP clients without polling.
tools.usage:
ch = CreateChannel[]
ch = CreateChannel["name"]
ch = CreateChannel["name", Permissions -> "Public"]
ChannelObject["user:name"]
DeleteChannel[ch]

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Channel path (relative to your cloud user).

tools.name: ChannelSend
tools.description: Sends a message (any expression, typically an association) to a channel identified by ChannelObject, name or URL; ChannelListeners on that channel receive it immediately. External programs can post to a public channel with a plain HTTP request to its URL, making it a simple event bus.
tools.usage:
ChannelSend[ch, msg]
ChannelSend["user:name", msg]
ChannelSend[url, msg]

tools.name: ChannelListen
tools.description: Starts listening on a channel, returning a ChannelListener whose handler function is called with each incoming message association ("Message", "Timestamp", "Sender" keys); with None messages are just accumulated. RemoveChannelListener stops it, ChannelListeners lists active listeners and ChannelReceiverFunction deploys a cloud-side handler that runs without a local kernel.
tools.usage:
listener = ChannelListen[ch, handler]
ChannelListen[ch, None]
listener["MessageList"]
RemoveChannelListener[listener]
ChannelListeners[]
CloudDeploy[ChannelReceiverFunction[handler], "receiver"]

parameters.name: handler
parameters.description: Function applied to each message association.

tools.example:
l = ChannelListen[ChannelObject["alerts"], Print[#Message] &];
(* ... later *)
l["MessageList"]
RemoveChannelListener[l]

tools.name: CreateDatabin
tools.description: Creates a Wolfram Data Drop databin (a cloud time-stamped data store with a short ID) returning a Databin object; DatabinAdd appends one entry (association or value) and DatabinUpload many at once, and Databins lists your bins. Anything from IoT devices to web forms can add entries via the bin's HTTP endpoint, and Databin[id] retrieves them as associations, TimeSeries or Dataset.
tools.usage:
bin = CreateDatabin[]
bin = CreateDatabin[<|"Name" -> "sensors", "Interpretation" -> {"temp" -> "Number"}|>]
DatabinAdd[bin, <|"temp" -> 21.5|>]
DatabinUpload[bin, {<|...|>, <|...|>}]
Databin["id"]
Databin["id", -10]
bin["TimeSeries"]
Databins[]

parameters.name: Interpretation
parameters.description: Creation option: Interpreter types applied to incoming fields.

tools.notes: Public bins accept anonymous entries at https://datadrop.wolframcloud.com/api/v1.0/Add?bin=ID&temp=22 - convenient for devices without a Wolfram kernel.

tools.name: SessionSubmit
tools.description: Submits an expression (or a ScheduledTask) for asynchronous evaluation in the current kernel session, returning a TaskObject immediately; the expression runs when the kernel is idle, with HandlerFunctions for completion/failure callbacks. Use it for background jobs and timers inside one kernel; LocalSubmit runs in a separate local kernel and CloudSubmit in the cloud.
tools.usage:
task = SessionSubmit[expr]
SessionSubmit[ScheduledTask[expr, Quantity[5, "Minutes"]]]
SessionSubmit[ScheduledTask[expr, {dt, n}]]
SessionSubmit[expr, HandlerFunctions -> <|"TaskFinished" -> f|>]
LocalSubmit[expr]
CloudSubmit[expr]
CloudSubmit[ScheduledTask[expr, "Daily"]]

parameters.name: HandlerFunctionsKeys
parameters.description: Option: which data keys the handlers receive ("EvaluationResult", "TaskUUID", ...).

tools.example:
task = SessionSubmit[ScheduledTask[Print["tick ", Now], {1, 5}]]
res = SessionSubmit[Integrate[Sin[x]^10, x], HandlerFunctions -> <|"TaskFinished" -> (Print[#EvaluationResult] &)|>]
LocalSubmit[Export["big.png", Plot3D[Sin[x y], {x, 0, 3}, {y, 0, 3}]]]
tools.notes: ScheduledTask schedule forms: a time quantity or seconds (repeat interval), {dt, n} (n repetitions), a DateObject (run once), {DateObject, dt}, named periods "Hourly"/"Daily"/"Weekly"/"Monthly", cron-style strings such as "0 9 * * MON", or lists of dates; cloud tasks (CloudSubmit/CloudDeploy) run without any local kernel.

tools.name: TaskObject
tools.description: Represents an asynchronous or scheduled task created by SessionSubmit, LocalSubmit, CloudSubmit, URLSubmit or ScheduledTask deployment; supports properties ("TaskStatus", "TaskType", "EvaluationResult", "RunCount", "NextRunTime") and the management functions TaskWait (block until done), TaskAbort, TaskSuspend, TaskResume, TaskRemove and Tasks (list all). Essential for controlling background work.
tools.usage:
task["TaskStatus"]
TaskWait[task]
TaskAbort[task]
TaskSuspend[task]
TaskResume[task]
TaskRemove[task]
Tasks[]
Tasks["Session"]
TaskExecute[task]

tools.name: ContinuousTask
tools.description: ContinuousTask[expr] submitted to the cloud (CloudSubmit) or a session keeps re-evaluating expr continuously (as fast as allowed, or with a time limit), for long-running listeners and pollers; contrast ScheduledTask, which runs at discrete times. Manage it through the returned TaskObject.
tools.usage:
CloudSubmit[ContinuousTask[expr]]
CloudSubmit[ContinuousTask[expr, timelimit]]
SessionSubmit[ContinuousTask[expr]]

parameters.name: timelimit
parameters.description: Maximum total run time (Quantity or seconds).

tools.name: LocalObject
tools.description: A file-backed local storage object (the local analogue of CloudObject): Put/Get, Export/Import, CopyFile and DeleteObject work on it, LocalObjects lists them and $LocalBase is their root directory. Use it for durable per-machine caches and results without managing file paths by hand.
tools.usage:
obj = LocalObject[]
obj = LocalObject["name"]
Put[expr, obj]
Get[obj]
Export[LocalObject["data"], data, "JSON"]
LocalObjects[]
$LocalBase

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Object name (path relative to $LocalBase); omitted for an anonymous UUID object.

tools.name: LocalSymbol
tools.description: LocalSymbol["name"] is a symbol whose value persists on the local machine across kernel sessions (stored under $LocalSymbolBase), the local counterpart of CloudSymbol; assign and read it like an ordinary symbol. Good for remembering settings, counters and last-run times between script executions.
tools.usage:
LocalSymbol["name"]
LocalSymbol["name"] = value
LocalSymbol["name"] =.
$LocalSymbolBase

tools.name: LocalCache
tools.description: LocalCache[obj] downloads a cloud object or URL to a local object once and returns the local copy on subsequent calls, giving transparent on-disk caching of remote data; LocalCache[obj, loc] chooses the location. Use it in scripts that repeatedly read large remote files.
tools.usage:
LocalCache[CloudObject["path"]]
LocalCache["https://example.com/big.csv"]
Import[LocalCache[url], "CSV"]

tools.name: PersistentSymbol
tools.description: PersistentSymbol["name"] is a symbol whose value persists across sessions in a chosen persistence location ("KernelSession", "FrontEndSession", "Notebook", "Local", "Cloud", "Installation"), searched in $PersistencePath order; it generalizes LocalSymbol and CloudSymbol (12.3+). PersistentObject / PersistentObjects give the underlying objects and PersistenceLocation names locations; InitializationValue sets a value applied automatically at kernel start-up.
tools.usage:
PersistentSymbol["name"]
PersistentSymbol["name", "Local"] = value
PersistentSymbol["name", "Cloud"]
PersistentObjects[]
PersistentObjects["name*", "Local"]
$PersistencePath
InitializationValue[symbol, "Local"] = value
InitializationValue[$Language] = "German"

parameters.name: loc
parameters.description: PersistenceLocation name or object; omitted searches $PersistencePath.

tools.example:
PersistentSymbol["apiToken", "Local"] = "abc123";
PersistentSymbol["apiToken"]
InitializationValue[$CharacterEncoding, "Local"] = "UTF-8"; (* applied at every kernel start *)
PersistentObjects["apiToken", "Local"]

tools.name: InitializationValue
tools.description: Sets a value for a symbol (often a system variable such as $Language, $CharacterEncoding, $Path additions) that is automatically assigned when a kernel starts, stored in a persistence location; InitializationObjects lists them and Initialization -> True on PersistentObject achieves the same. It replaces hand-edited init.m files for simple start-up settings.
tools.usage:
InitializationValue[symbol] = value
InitializationValue[symbol, loc] = value
InitializationValue[symbol] =.
InitializationObjects[]

tools.name: EvaluationData
tools.description: Evaluates an expression and returns an association with the result plus metadata: "Result", "Success", "Messages", "MessagesText", "Timing", "AbsoluteTiming", "FailureType" - the same structure cloud APIs and tasks report. Use it to capture complete diagnostics of an evaluation in one call, e.g. for logging in batch jobs.
tools.usage:
EvaluationData[expr]
EvaluationData[expr]["Messages"]
tools.example:
ed = EvaluationData[Quiet[1/0]];
ed["Result"] (* ComplexInfinity *)
ed["MessagesText"]
ed["AbsoluteTiming"]

tools.name: CreateUUID
tools.description: Generates a random universally unique identifier string (optionally with a prefix), as used for cloud object names, task IDs, databin entries and session tokens. Use it wherever unique keys are needed for files, records or temporary cloud objects.
tools.usage:
CreateUUID[]
CreateUUID["prefix"]

tools.name: $CloudBase
tools.description: The base URL of the cloud the session connects to (https://www.wolframcloud.com/ by default, or an Enterprise Private Cloud); $CloudUserID / $WolframID identify the user, $WolframUUID the account UUID, $CloudConnected whether a connection exists, $CloudSymbolBase and $CloudExpressionBase the default storage roots, and $EvaluationCloudObject / $CloudEvaluation / $RequesterAddress / $RequesterWolframID describe the context when code runs inside a deployed cloud object.
tools.usage:
$CloudBase
$CloudBase = "https://cloud.mycompany.com/"
$CloudUserID
$WolframID
$CloudConnected
$CloudEvaluation
$RequesterWolframID
$EvaluationCloudObject
tools.example:
CloudDeploy[APIFunction[{}, <|"caller" -> $RequesterWolframID, "ip" -> $RequesterAddress, "object" -> $EvaluationCloudObject|> &], Permissions -> "Public"]
If[$CloudEvaluation, Print["running in the cloud"]]

tools.name: DeleteObject
tools.description: Deletes cloud objects, local objects, databins, channels, external sessions, tasks and other managed objects (the generic destructor for object types that hold external resources); DeleteFile is for plain files and DeleteDirectory for directories. Always call it on StartExternalSession / web sessions when done.
tools.usage:
DeleteObject[obj]
DeleteObject[{obj1, obj2, ...}]

parameters.name: obj
parameters.description: CloudObject, LocalObject, Databin, ChannelObject, ExternalSessionObject, WebSessionObject, TaskObject, ...

tools.name: CloudObjectNameFormat
tools.description: Option of CloudDeploy, CloudPut, CloudPublish etc. controlling how object names are turned into URLs ("UUID", "UserURLBase", "CloudUserID", "CloudUserUUID"), and CloudObjectURLType chooses the URL scheme ("Object" for /obj/ paths, "Environment" for /env/); together with CloudObjectNameFormat they decide whether deployed URLs expose the user name. Set them for stable, shareable API URLs.
tools.usage:
CloudDeploy[expr, "name", CloudObjectNameFormat -> "UUID"]
CloudDeploy[expr, "name", CloudObjectURLType -> "Environment"]
SetOptions[CloudDeploy, CloudObjectNameFormat -> "UserURLBase"]
